searchText: IIUC, there is the following chain: `A <- B (invalid) <- C <- D` 1) `CL: FCU(B), EL: {status: INVALID, lvh: A}` 2) `CL: newPayload(C), EL: SYNCING` as the `B` might have been discarded because it is invalid 3) `CL: FCU(C) or newPayload(D), EL: {status: INVALID, lvh: A}` This is how i see it from the spec perspective, don't want to speculate on the implementations behaviour, but they also can potentially respond `CL: newPayload(C), EL: {status: INVALID, lvh: A}` as they know that `C.parent == B` and `B` is invalid Agree with your description. Looking at the code, I think Besu may actually respond with either SYNCING or INVALID depending on how the parent was invalid 🥴 you mean depending on what exact check has failed? yeh it looks like if it's something akin to a 400 like missing/bad request data we don't remember the block, whereas we do if it's invalid during block processing. We could fairly easily fix it to always return invalid I reckon, if it's an issue for CLs. Maybe there's some nuance if the block is technically valid but engine api data isn't 🤔 Hmm, I was counting with the same spec reading as Misha above and I am moving Prysm to potentially ignore the FCU return from C in some cases, but if the EL will continue returning SYNCING on that chain instead of INVALID, we'd be bricked and being optimistic I am confused. There would be no `FCU(C)` if after `INVALID` response to `FCU(B)` prysm invalidated `B`, so you have to ignore `FCU(B)` to be able to ignore `FCU(C)`. Yes I'm moving to ignore the result of some FCU because we're going to be calling it async My understanding is that all ELs today actually reply valid/invalid if they can sync the block on new payload even if it's not canonical. In fact I'm not going to ignore it, but it will leave Prysm in a funky place of removing the forkchoice node async So I want to know the consequences of having this node even if temporarily

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
IIUC, there is the following chain: `A <- B (invalid) <- C <- D`
1) `CL: FCU(B), EL: {status: INVALID, lvh: A}`
2) `CL: newPayload(C), EL: SYNCING` as the `B` might have been discarded because it is invalid
3) `CL: FCU(C) or newPayload(D), EL: {status: INVALID, lvh: A}`

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: This is how i see it from the spec perspective, don't want to speculate on the implementations behaviour, but they also can potentially respond `CL: newPayload(C), EL: {status: INVALID, lvh: A}` as they know that `C.parent == B` and `B` is invalid

excerpts.content: Agree with your description. Looking at the code, I think Besu may actually respond with either SYNCING or INVALID depending on how the parent was invalid 🥴

We could fairly easily fix it to always return invalid I reckon, if it's an issue for CLs. Maybe there's some nuance if the block is technically valid but engine api data isn't 🤔
